interest: Perry commemorations as 1930s peace diplomacy: Grew's diary, press clippings, and State's refusal of a destroyer visit to Shimoda.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.415, File 816) comprises 51 documents spanning 1932 to 1939 (predominantly 1934) that document commemorative events, historical celebrations, and bilateral memorial observances between the United States and Japan. While the collection includes early items concerning reciprocal agreements to end official wreath-laying on war memorials, an Armistice Day goodwill visit by Tokyo Boy Scouts, late-1930s efforts to secure restricted Japanese shipbuilding histories, and memorial tributes honoring Japanese-American relations advocate Wallace McKinney Alexander, the vast majority of the record centers on the March–May 1934 nationwide observances marking the 80th anniversary of Commodore Matthew C. Perry’s 1854 Treaty of Kanagawa. Through extensive diplomatic reporting by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, department instructions from Secretary of State Cordell Hull, and exchanges with Japanese civic, commercial, and press organizations, the file details civic banquets across Tokyo, Kobe, Nagoya, and Naha, the Black Ship Festival at Shimoda, trans-Pacific radio broadcasts, and the delicate management of bilateral goodwill rhetoric.
